No appearance  ORDER

The Criminal Revision is filed against the order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Tambaram, in Crl.MO.No.7329 of 2022 in CC.No.222 of 2020 dated 05.12.2022.
2.

It is the case of the prosecution that the defacto complainant Thangabai had lodged a complaint during March 2017 before the Commissioner of Police, Greater Chennai against the respondents 2 &
3.

The first respondent has registered a case against the respondents 2 & 3 for the offences under Section 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of IPC and filed charge sheet before the learned Judicial Magistrate-I, Tambaram in CC.No.222 of 2020.
During trial, the respondent police has filed a petition before the designated Court under Section 319 Cr.P.C. to implead the petitioner as accused in this case and the same was allowed.
Challenging the said order, the petitioner/accused has filed the present revision before this Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3
. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner submitted that except the deposition of PW1 and PW2, there is no other document evidence to show that the petitioner is involved in this case.
The respondent police has not produced any documentary evidence neither before the trial Court or before this Court.

The petitioner has acted as an agent and mere participation of the petitioner during settlement and in the absence of any evidence, the trial Court allowed the petition and added the petitioner as an accused in this case, which is not sustainable.
This Court may interfere with the impugned order passed by the trial Court and quash the same by allowing this petition.

4. The Government Advocate submitted that based on the evidence of PW1 and PW2, Section 319 petition was filed by the respondent police to implead the petitioner as accused and the same was allowed, which cannot be interfered with.

5. The learned counsel for the 4th respondent/defacto complainant submitted that except the deposition of PW1 and PW2, no sufficient documentary evidence is available to prove the allegation as against the petitioner.

The PW1 and PW2 have deposed that on instigation of Sivaji Rao,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the offence appears to have been committed by A1 and A2.
The trail Court has found prima facie, allowed the petition and added the petitioner as an accused.
However, the petitioner has to prove his innocense only at the time of trial before the trial Court.
Filing the present revision is pre-
matured and the same has to be dismissed.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate and the learned counsel for the 4th respondent and perused the materials available on record.
7.

A careful perusal of the impugned order which reveals that the court below has taken into consideration the deposition of evidence of PW1 and PW2, had come to the conclusion that the petitioner appears to have involved in the crime.
On assumption, PW1 and PW2 has mentioned the petitioners name.

Except that, no other witness or documentary evidence is available to show that B.Shivaji Rao vs The Inspector Of Police on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49560048/
2 the petitioner is involved in the crime.
